name: Kikai-jima Ryukyuan, Wan dialect

catalog_quote: 名詞の型の一覧を（7）に示す。アクセント単位が長くなっても 2 種類の対立しかない「二型アクセント」である。両系列を α／β と名付ける［…］ただし，1 拍語は α 系列の 1 種類のみである［…］α 系列は単語レベルでも文節レベルでも同じで，単語は裸の文節でもあるので，「文節がアクセント単位になり，その次末拍のみが低まる」と記述される。それに対して β 系列は単語レベルでの指定が必要で，（/[/）「単語の次末拍（−②）に昇り核がある」と解釈する。昇り核のある拍で高くなり，その後は，接続形ではそのまま「文節」の最後まで高く続くのに対して，言い切り形では文節末拍で下がる。［…］β 系列との対比上，α 系列は無核型と認められる［…］補足すると，β 系列の単語に固有なのは上昇（[）であり，下降（]）は単語に固有の属性ではない。 (pp. 51–53) — English abstract, p. 75: "the Wan dialect, which has a two-pattern accent system, one pattern with word-tone on the bunsetsu unit, and one pattern with an ascending kernel on the penultimate mora of the word. Here we see coexistence of word-tone and accent kernel. It also has the peculiarity that a moraic nasal can bear a final high pitch of the word-tone, but not an ascending kernel."

new_statements.quote: 名詞の型の一覧を（7）に示す。アクセント単位が長くなっても 2 種類の対立しかない「二型アクセント」である。両系列を α／β と名付ける［…］α 系列は単語レベルでも文節レベルでも同じで，単語は裸の文節でもあるので，「文節がアクセント単位になり，その次末拍のみが低まる」と記述される。それに対して β 系列は単語レベルでの指定が必要で，「単語の次末拍（−②）に昇り核がある」と解釈する。昇り核のある拍で高くなり，その後は，接続形ではそのまま「文節」の最後まで高く続くのに対して，言い切り形では文節末拍で下がる。［…］β 系列との対比上，α 系列は無核型と認められる
new_statements.translation: The list of noun patterns is given in (7). It is a 'two-pattern accent' with only two contrasting types no matter how long the accent unit becomes. I call the two series α/β [...] The α series is the same at word level and at bunsetsu (phrase) level, and since a word is also a bare bunsetsu, it is described as 'the bunsetsu is the accent unit and only its penultimate mora is lowered'. The β series, by contrast, needs a word-level specification, and is interpreted as 'having a rising kernel on the penultimate mora (−2) of the word'. The pitch rises at the kernel mora; after that, in the connective form it stays high to the end of the bunsetsu, whereas in the final (citation) form it falls on the last mora of the bunsetsu. [...] In contrast to the β series, the α series is recognised as the kernelless type. (English abstract, p. 75: 'the Wan dialect, which has a two-pattern accent system, one pattern with word-tone on the bunsetsu unit, and one pattern with an ascending kernel on the penultimate mora of the word.')

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kikai has an N-pattern (Ryukyuan-type) pitch accent, not stress. Each lexical item belongs to one of a small fixed number of accent series (two in Uwano 2012: α/β; Uwano 2016 and the NINJAL data papers add a third, γ). The pitch shape is fixed by the series and counted from the right edge: α = kernelless, the whole bunsetsu (noun + particles) is high except its penultimate mora, which is low; β = an obligatory pitch rise on the penultimate mora of the word (-2), high to the end of the phrase in connective form, with a fall on the phrase-final mora in citation form; γ = the rise on the antepenultimate mora (-3), 3+-mora words only. Mora (not syllable) is the counting unit. Nothing is said of stress/intensity; the description is entirely pitch/tonal.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not applicable; no secondary prominence is described. Uwano notes (pp. 52–53) that in the β series only the rise is lexical, the final fall being a phrase-final intonational feature.
new_statements.exceptions: One-mora (long-vowel) nouns are all α (p. 52); the moraic nasal can carry the α word-tone's final high but not a β rising kernel (abstract p. 75). Uwano 2016 p. 95 revises the 2012 two-pattern analysis of central/southern dialects to three-pattern after a γ pattern was found in loanwords and place names (mostly words with a moraic nasal/geminate in the penult); the northern Onotsu dialect is three-pattern and additionally sensitive to word length (≤3, 4, >4 morae) and special morae (Uwano 2016 pp. 97, 109). Shirata 2016 (abstract) analyses Kamikatetsu as a two-pattern system with accentedness lexically specified per morpheme and an HLH* melody.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the bunsetsu (word + following particles) for the α series and the word for the β/γ kernels; citation (言い切り) and connective (接続) forms differ for β/γ (final fall vs. sustained high). Data are elicited nouns in isolation and with particles; the Wan dialect (central Kikai, the most widespread type) is the reference variety, with Sakamine, Kamikatetsu, Araki, Nakasato and Isaneku compared.
new_statements.identity_note: Kikai (kika1239) is not a single accent system: the quoted statement describes the central/southern type, exemplified by the Wan dialect (the most widespread type on the island; Sakamine, Kamikatetsu, Araki, Nakasato, Isaneku described alongside), which Uwano 2012 analyses as two-pattern and Uwano 2016 revises to three-pattern (α/β/γ). The northern villages Onotsu, Shitooke and Sateku have a distinct three-pattern system with word-length and special-mora constraints (Uwano 2016; Uwano 2002b). Shirata 2016 (Kamikatetsu, southernmost village) analyses that variety as two-pattern with morpheme-level accentedness. No separate Glottolog codes exist for these dialect groups; all fall under kika1239.

tone_statements.citation: 白田理人 (Shirata, Rihito). 2021. 呼びかけイントネーションが呼称名詞に与える影響―喜界島小野津方言を例に― [Influence of vocative intonation on address nouns: the case of the Onotsu dialect of Kikai Ryukyuan]. 音声研究 (Journal of the Phonetic Society of Japan) 25: 23–40. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.25.0_23
tone_statements.quote: ここでは，上野（2016）に基づいて小野津方言のアクセント体系を概観する。小野津方言は，上野（1989, p. 202，1992, p. 11）において「そこで昇ろうとする力」と規定されている「昇り核」の有無と位置で区別されるα型・β型・γ型からなる三型アクセント体系を持つ 8）。それぞれの型の特徴は（1）の通りである。α 型／β 型で 3 拍目以降に核がある場合と無核型であるγ型において語頭拍が高くなるほかは，基本的に核の置かれた拍のみが高くなり，それ以外は低くなる ... （1） α型・β型・γ型の特徴（cf. 上野 2016） i. α型―昇り核が次末拍にある型 ... ii. β型―昇り核が末尾拍にある型 ... iii. γ型―無核型
tone_statements.translation: Here, following Uwano (2016), I outline the accent system of the Onotsu dialect. Onotsu has a three-pattern accent system consisting of types α, β and γ, distinguished by the presence and position of an 'ascending kernel', defined by Uwano (1989: 202, 1992: 11) as 'a force to rise at that point'. The features of each type are as in (1). Apart from the word-initial mora becoming high when the kernel is on the 3rd mora or later in α/β and in the kernel-less γ type, basically only the mora bearing the kernel is high and the rest are low ... (1) i. α: kernel on the penultimate mora; ii. β: kernel on the final mora; iii. γ: kernel-less type.
tone_statements.locator: p. 25, sec. 2.3 アクセント and example (1); mora statement p. 26
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern (N-kei) word-accent system with an ascending kernel counted in morae, not syllables (p. 26); alpha/beta types shift the kernel onto following particles. Adds a fourth type, delta, for address nouns, with Praat pitch tracks (figs. 2-6). Overview credited to Uwano 2016. No stress.

tone_statements.citation: 白田理人 (Shirata, Rihito). 2020. 喜界島方言における動詞のアクセント単位の拡張と真偽疑問文末のプロソディー [Extension of the verbal accent unit and polar-question-final prosody in the Kikai-jima dialects]. 日本言語学会第161回大会予稿集 (Proceedings of the 161st Meeting of the Linguistic Society of Japan), 2020-11-21. 日本言語学会.
tone_statements.quote: 上野・西岡（1995）に基づき，小野津方言／上嘉鉄方言の動詞のアクセントを表 1 にまとめて示す。...表に示す通り，小野津方言／上嘉鉄方言ともに，I ／ II の二つの系列が区別される。小野津方言では，系列 I は 2 拍目が，系列 II は末尾拍が上昇する（ただし，系列 I の 2 拍語は語頭が上昇し，系列 II の 5 拍語は次末拍が上昇する）。一方，上嘉鉄方言では，系列 I は末尾拍が，系列 II は次末拍が上昇する。
tone_statements.translation: Based on Uwano & Nishioka (1995), Table 1 summarizes the verb accent of the Onotsu and Kamikatetsu dialects. ... As the table shows, in both the Onotsu and the Kamikatetsu dialect two series, I and II, are distinguished. In Onotsu, series I rises on the 2nd mora and series II on the final mora (except that 2-mora words of series I rise word-initially and 5-mora words of series II rise on the penultimate mora). In Kamikatetsu, by contrast, series I rises on the final mora and series II on the penultimate mora.
tone_statements.locator: p. 383, section 2.1 動詞アクセント
tone_statements.summary: Onotsu and Kamikatetsu verbs: two lexical accent series, each a pitch rise on a mora fixed by series and word length, in an accent unit that can extend onto final particles; in Onotsu a geminate/long-vowel mora cannot bear the rise. Own fieldwork; Table 1 after Uwano & Nishioka 1995. No stress.

tone_statements.citation: 上野善道 (Uwano, Zendo). 2017. 喜界島小野津方言の地名複合語アクセント資料 [Accent data on place-name compounds in the Onotsu dialect of Kikai-jima]. 南島文化 (Bulletin of the Institute of Ryukyuan Culture) 39: 85–102. 宜野湾: 沖縄国際大学南島文化研究所. hdl:2308/1063 (https://okiu1972.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/1021)
tone_statements.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核 /[/ が単語の次末拍にある次末核（−②），β系列は同じく語末核（−①），γ系列は無核（⓪）で，それらに語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。その上に，語形の長さや特殊拍の種類に応じた交替があって複雑になっているが，語頭の上昇範囲のゆれも含めて，詳細は上記拙論に譲る。
tone_statements.translation: The Onotsu dialect has a three-pattern accent consisting of the three series α, β, γ. The α series has a penultimate kernel (−2), i.e. the rising kernel /[/ is on the word's second-to-last mora; the β series likewise has a word-final kernel (−1); the γ series is kernel-less (0); over these is laid a shape feature whereby the beginning of the word rises. On top of that there are alternations depending on word length and the kind of special mora, which make it complex, but for the details, including variation in the extent of the initial rise, I refer to my paper cited above [Uwano 2016].
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern pitch accent: lexical classes α (rising kernel on penultimate mora), β (kernel on final mora), γ (unaccented), plus a word-initial rise; p. 86: compound rules (pattern set by second member); pp. 87-102: pitch-marked compounds, one speaker. Details left to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: 上野善道 (Uwano, Zendo). 2017. 喜界島小野津方言の外来語アクセント資料 [Accent data on loanwords in the Onotsu dialect of Kikai-jima]. 琉球の方言 41: 91–117 (査読付き論文). Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00014497, hdl:10114/13848
tone_statements.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核/［/が単語の次末拍にある次末核（－②），β系列は同じく語末核（－①），γ系列は無核（＠）で，第３モーラ以降に核がある場合と無核型には，語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。詳細は拙文（2016）を参照のこと。ただし，以下では「系列」は「型」とまとめて呼ぶ。
tone_statements.translation: The Onotsu dialect has a three-pattern accent consisting of the three series α, β, γ. The α series has a rising kernel /［/ on the penultimate mora of the word (penultimate kernel, -②), the β series likewise a word-final kernel (-①), and the γ series is kernelless (＠); when the kernel is on the third mora or later, and in the kernelless type, a word-initial rising shape feature is overlaid. For details see my 2016 paper. Below, however, the 'series' are collectively called 'types'.
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern word accent: α = rising kernel on the penultimate mora, β = kernel on the final mora, γ = kernelless, with an initial rise overlaid; kernel shifts before particles. Data paper: 1549 accent-marked loanwords from one speaker b. 1927; analysis deferred to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: 上野善道・西岡敏 (Uwano, Zendo & Nishioka, Satoshi). 1995. 喜界島方言の動詞継続相のアクセント [Accent of the verb continuative aspect in the Kikai-jima dialects]. 琉球の方言 (Ryūkyū no Hōgen) 18–19 (中本正智博士追悼号): 145–163. Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00012660, hdl:10114/11994
tone_statements.quote: 喜界島諸方言の名詞のアクセント体系は、その音調型に集落差が大きく、類の統合の仕方にも違いがあるものの、佐手久(さでく)集落の3型アクセントを除けば、いずれも「2型アクセント」である。... Ⅱの言い切り形と接続形は音韻的に同形で、ともに「単語」(名詞)の次末拍(語末から2拍目, −②)に核があり、そこが高くなる。... 一方、Ⅰは「文節」の次末拍だけが「低」という規則で決まる無核型(@)である。... これを含めると、湾方言は、単語レベルでは@型、−②型、−③型の「3型アクセント」の体系ということになる。そして小野津を除く他の諸方言もまた、動詞を含めた全体としては3型アクセントと認定される。
tone_statements.translation: The noun accent systems of the Kikai-jima dialects differ greatly between villages in their pitch patterns and in how the (accent) classes have merged, but apart from the three-pattern accent of Sateku village they are all 'two-pattern accent' systems. ... The conclusive and connective forms of II are phonologically identical: both have the kernel on the penultimate mora (2nd mora from the end, -2) of the 'word' (noun), which becomes high. ... I, by contrast, is the kernel-less type (@ = 0), fixed by the rule that only the penultimate mora of the 'bunsetsu' is low. ... Including this, the Wan dialect is, at word level, a 'three-pattern accent' system with types 0, -2 and -3. And the other dialects except Onotsu are likewise recognised as three-pattern accent systems once verbs are included.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: N-pattern word-pitch accent: nouns show two accent patterns per village (Sateku three); Wan is analysed with a rising kernel (昇り核) on the penultimate mora vs a kernel-less type, high/low per mora; verb continuative forms add an antepenult-kernel type, so three patterns at word level. No stress data.

sources.note: Wan dialect (central Kikai) has a two-pattern (N-type) pitch accent: alpha series = phrase(bunsetsu)-level word-tone with only the penultimate mora low (kernelless); beta series = rising kernel on the penultimate mora of the word; five other central/southern dialects (Sakamine, Kamikatetsu, Araki, Nakasato, Isaneku) described relative to Wan (pp. 51–53, 75).

sources.citation: 上野善道 (Uwano, Zendo). 2016. 喜界島小野津方言のアクセント体系—外来語と地名語彙から見る—. 音声研究 (Journal of the Phonetic Society of Japan) 20(3): 95–111.
sources.note: p. 95: earlier view was central/south = two-pattern, north = three-pattern; a third (gamma) pattern has since been found in central/south too, so they are three-pattern; p. 97 (4) Nakasato: alpha = bunsetsu-domain, penultimate mora low (kernelless); beta = rising kernel on word penultimate mora (-2); gamma = rising kernel on antepenultimate mora (-3, 3+ mora words only); p. 109: Onotsu (north) confirmed three-pattern, sensitive to word length and special morae.

sources.note: Data volumes for central/southern dialects (Nakasato, Sakamine, Kamikatetsu): (4) abstract reports a third (gamma) pattern in nouns, so nouns as well as verbs are three-pattern (alpha/beta/gamma); (5) loanword accent, three patterns with heavy skew toward beta.

tone.translation: Here, following Uwano (2016), I outline the accent system of the Onotsu dialect. Onotsu has a three-pattern accent system consisting of types α, β and γ, distinguished by the presence and position of an 'ascending kernel', defined by Uwano (1989: 202, 1992: 11) as 'a force to rise at that point'. The features of each type are as in (1). Apart from the word-initial mora becoming high when the kernel is on the 3rd mora or later in α/β and in the kernel-less γ type, basically only the mora bearing the kernel is high and the rest are low ... (1) i. α: kernel on the penultimate mora; ii. β: kernel on the final mora; iii. γ: kernel-less type.
tone.summary: Three-pattern (N-kei) word-accent system with an ascending kernel counted in morae, not syllables (p. 26); alpha/beta types shift the kernel onto following particles. Adds a fourth type, delta, for address nouns, with Praat pitch tracks (figs. 2-6). Overview credited to Uwano 2016. No stress.

sources.quote: 上野・西岡（1995）に基づき，小野津方言／上嘉鉄方言の動詞のアクセントを表 1 にまとめて示す。...表に示す通り，小野津方言／上嘉鉄方言ともに，I ／ II の二つの系列が区別される。小野津方言では，系列 I は 2 拍目が，系列 II は末尾拍が上昇する（ただし，系列 I の 2 拍語は語頭が上昇し，系列 II の 5 拍語は次末拍が上昇する）。一方，上嘉鉄方言では，系列 I は末尾拍が，系列 II は次末拍が上昇する。

tone.translation: Based on Uwano & Nishioka (1995), Table 1 summarizes the verb accent of the Onotsu and Kamikatetsu dialects. ... As the table shows, in both the Onotsu and the Kamikatetsu dialect two series, I and II, are distinguished. In Onotsu, series I rises on the 2nd mora and series II on the final mora (except that 2-mora words of series I rise word-initially and 5-mora words of series II rise on the penultimate mora). In Kamikatetsu, by contrast, series I rises on the final mora and series II on the penultimate mora.

Own fieldwork; Table 1 after Uwano & Nishioka 1995. No stress.

sources.citation: 上野善道 (Uwano, Zendo). 2017. 喜界島小野津方言の地名複合語アクセント資料 [Accent data on place-name compounds in the Onotsu dialect of Kikai-jima]. 南島文化 (Bulletin of the Institute of Ryukyuan Culture) 39: 85–102. 宜野湾: 沖縄国際大学南島文化研究所. hdl:2308/1063 (https://okiu1972.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/1021)
sources.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核 /[/ が単語の次末拍にある次末核（−②），β系列は同じく語末核（−①），γ系列は無核（⓪）で，それらに語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。その上に，語形の長さや特殊拍の種類に応じた交替があって複雑になっているが，語頭の上昇範囲のゆれも含めて，詳細は上記拙論に譲る。
sources.note: Three-pattern pitch accent: lexical classes α (rising kernel on penultimate mora), β (kernel on final mora), γ (unaccented), plus a word-initial rise; p. 86: compound rules (pattern set by second member); pp. 87-102: pitch-marked compounds, one speaker. Details left to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

tone.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核 /[/ が単語の次末拍にある次末核（−②），β系列は同じく語末核（−①），γ系列は無核（⓪）で，それらに語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。その上に，語形の長さや特殊拍の種類に応じた交替があって複雑になっているが，語頭の上昇範囲のゆれも含めて，詳細は上記拙論に譲る。
tone.translation: The Onotsu dialect has a three-pattern accent consisting of the three series α, β, γ. The α series has a penultimate kernel (−2), i.e. the rising kernel /[/ is on the word's second-to-last mora; the β series likewise has a word-final kernel (−1); the γ series is kernel-less (0); over these is laid a shape feature whereby the beginning of the word rises. On top of that there are alternations depending on word length and the kind of special mora, which make it complex, but for the details, including variation in the extent of the initial rise, I refer to my paper cited above [Uwano 2016].
tone.summary: Three-pattern pitch accent: lexical classes α (rising kernel on penultimate mora), β (kernel on final mora), γ (unaccented), plus a word-initial rise; p. 86: compound rules (pattern set by second member); pp. 87-102: pitch-marked compounds, one speaker. Details left to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

sources.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核/［/が単語の次末拍にある次末核（－②），β系列は同じく語末核（－①），γ系列は無核（＠）で，第３モーラ以降に核がある場合と無核型には，語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。詳細は拙文（2016）を参照のこと。ただし，以下では「系列」は「型」とまとめて呼ぶ。
sources.note: Three-pattern word accent: α = rising kernel on the penultimate mora, β = kernel on the final mora, γ = kernelless, with an initial rise overlaid; kernel shifts before particles. Data paper: 1549 accent-marked loanwords from one speaker b. 1927; analysis deferred to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

tone.quote: 小野津方言は，α，β，γの３系列からなる三型アクセントである。α系列は昇り核/［/が単語の次末拍にある次末核（－②），β系列は同じく語末核（－①），γ系列は無核（＠）で，第３モーラ以降に核がある場合と無核型には，語頭が上昇する形状特徴が被さる。詳細は拙文（2016）を参照のこと。ただし，以下では「系列」は「型」とまとめて呼ぶ。
tone.translation: The Onotsu dialect has a three-pattern accent consisting of the three series α, β, γ. The α series has a rising kernel /［/ on the penultimate mora of the word (penultimate kernel, -②), the β series likewise a word-final kernel (-①), and the γ series is kernelless (＠); when the kernel is on the third mora or later, and in the kernelless type, a word-initial rising shape feature is overlaid. For details see my 2016 paper. Below, however, the 'series' are collectively called 'types'.
tone.summary: Three-pattern word accent: α = rising kernel on the penultimate mora, β = kernel on the final mora, γ = kernelless, with an initial rise overlaid; kernel shifts before particles. Data paper: 1549 accent-marked loanwords from one speaker b. 1927; analysis deferred to Uwano 2016. Nothing on stress.

sources.quote: 喜界島諸方言の名詞のアクセント体系は、その音調型に集落差が大きく、類の統合の仕方にも違いがあるものの、佐手久(さでく)集落の3型アクセントを除けば、いずれも「2型アクセント」である。... Ⅱの言い切り形と接続形は音韻的に同形で、ともに「単語」(名詞)の次末拍(語末から2拍目, −②)に核があり、そこが高くなる。... 一方、Ⅰは「文節」の次末拍だけが「低」という規則で決まる無核型(@)である。... これを含めると、湾方言は、単語レベルでは@型、−②型、−③型の「3型アクセント」の体系ということになる。そして小野津を除く他の諸方言もまた、動詞を含めた全体としては3型アクセントと認定される。
sources.note: N-pattern word-pitch accent: nouns show two accent patterns per village (Sateku three); Wan is analysed with a rising kernel (昇り核) on the penultimate mora vs a kernel-less type, high/low per mora; verb continuative forms add an antepenult-kernel type, so three patterns at word level. No stress data.

tone.translation: The noun accent systems of the Kikai-jima dialects differ greatly between villages in their pitch patterns and in how the (accent) classes have merged, but apart from the three-pattern accent of Sateku village they are all 'two-pattern accent' systems. ... The conclusive and connective forms of II are phonologically identical: both have the kernel on the penultimate mora (2nd mora from the end, -2) of the 'word' (noun), which becomes high. ... I, by contrast, is the kernel-less type (@ = 0), fixed by the rule that only the penultimate mora of the 'bunsetsu' is low. ... Including this, the Wan dialect is, at word level, a 'three-pattern accent' system with types 0, -2 and -3. And the other dialects except Onotsu are likewise recognised as three-pattern accent systems once verbs are included.

No stress data.

tone.quote: 以下には，喜界島諸方言のアクセントデータを掲載する。基礎語彙１データ・基礎語彙２データでは，音調の上がり目を [ で，音調の下がり目を ] で表記したが，ここでは見やすさを考えて，音調をあらわす記号として以下のものを使用する。高く発音される拍●： 高く発音される助詞の拍：▲ 低く発音される拍：○ 低く発音される助詞の拍：△ 中程度の高さで発音される拍：◎ ... 複数の型が回答された場合は，２つ（またはそれ以上）の型を / で区切って併記する。

tone.translation: Below we present the accent data of the Kikai-jima dialects. In the Basic Vocabulary 1 and 2 data a rise in pitch was written with [ and a fall in pitch with ], but here, for legibility, the following symbols are used to represent pitch: mora pronounced high ●; particle mora pronounced high ▲; mora pronounced low ○; particle mora pronounced low △; mora pronounced at mid height ◎ ... When more than one pattern was given in response, the two (or more) patterns are listed side by side separated by /.

tone.quote: 先に，拙文（1997）において，奄美・喜界島方言の8地点を取り上げ，その用言の活用形のアクセントを報告した。...今回は，そのうちの，湾を中心とする4地点を対象とする。...掲載の形式は前稿と基本的に同じである。注意すべき記号は次のとおりで，特に，音調の上昇と下降は，前稿のそれぞれ「と」から［と］に変更してある。［=上昇，］=下降，!=中レベル，'=声門閉鎖音，P,T,C,K=無気喉頭緊張音
tone.translation: Earlier, in my paper (1997), I took up eight localities of the Amami Kikai-jima dialects and reported the accent of the conjugated forms of their verbs and adjectives. ... This time four of those localities, centred on Wan, are treated. ... The format is basically the same as in the previous paper. The symbols to note are as follows; in particular, pitch rise and fall have been changed from the previous paper's 「 and 」 to [ and ]. [ = rise, ] = fall, ! = mid level, ' = glottal stop, P,T,C,K = unaspirated laryngeally tense consonants.
